changes_vs_current: New topic, no current list. Computed order (average position across the 4 people sources; missing = list length + 5): 1 Franklin 5.75, 2 Edison 6.25, 3 Bell 8.0, 4 Einstein 10.0, 5 Musk 10.25, 6 Gates 11.25, 7 Newton 12.25, 8 Wright Brothers 12.25, 9 Curie 12.5, 10 Jobs 12.5, 11 Nobel 13.0, 12 da Vinci 13.5, 13 Ford 13.75, 14 Tesla 13.75, 15 Gutenberg 15.5, 16 Pasteur 16.75, 17 Hedy Lamarr 16.75, 18 Salk 17.25, 19 Galileo 17.5, 20 Archimedes 17.75, 21 John Deere 17.75, 22 Eli Whitney 17.75, 23 Wozniak 17.75, 24 Berners-Lee 18.25, 25 Morse 18.75 ... 28 Carver 19.25. This order is skewed. The two fame sources (YouGov fame, pageviews) reward general celebrity: Musk, Gates, Newton, Curie and Nobel are famous for things other than invention. The two naming sources (Lemelson, Sporcle) each cover a fixed short set, so Tesla, Ford, Jobs, da Vinci and Einstein take a missing-item penalty in Sporcle, and Wright/Gutenberg/Whitney/Carver take one in YouGov, which has no ratings page for them. Gut-check moves: Edison 2->1 (Lemelson #1 by a wide margin, top 11 in every source, and the TIME/Qualcomm 2013 naming poll is widely reported with Edison first, though that page could not be opened, so it is not counted); Franklin 1->2; Bell stays 3; Wright Brothers 8->4 (Sporcle #2, its YouGov penalty is only a missing page); Tesla 14->5 (pageviews #6 and fame 82%; its penalties are fixed-set gaps; Pantheon #2); Ford 13->6 (YouGov fame 94%, pageviews #12, Sporcle First Names 88%); Jobs 10->7 (Lemelson #2, pageviews #3); da Vinci 12->8 (pageviews #9, fame 92%, Pantheon #1); Einstein 4->9 (he tops the fame data, but he is a physicist, so held just below the core inventors); Gutenberg 15->10; Eli Whitney 22->11 (Sporcle #5, a staple of US schooling, low pageviews); George Washington Carver 28->12 (gut check; pageviews #20, ahead of Gutenberg and Whitney; only 1 source covers him). Moved down because of these moves: Musk 5->13, Gates 6->14, Newton 7->15, Nobel 11->16, Curie 9->17. Tail: Morse 25->18 (Sporcle #10, a classic 'inventor of the telegraph'); Wozniak 23->19; Berners-Lee 24->20; Lamarr 17->21; Galileo 19->22; Pasteur 16->23; Archimedes 20->24. Dropped from the computed top 24: Jonas Salk (18; vaccine developer, rarely called an inventor) and John Deere (21; YouGov fame mostly reflects the brand).
confidence: Medium-high for 1-8 (Edison, Franklin, Bell, Wright Brothers, Tesla, Ford, Jobs and da Vinci are clearly the core, though their exact order is judgment). Medium for 9-12. Low-medium for 13-24, which lean on fame data and could equally include Zuckerberg, Salk, John Deere, Karl Benz, Erno Rubik, Samuel Colt, James Watt, Marconi or Madam C.J. Walker. Caveat: no US poll that asks adults to freely name inventors could be opened (TIME/Qualcomm 2013 unaided naming, Edison 27% > Einstein 9% > Bell 5% > da Vinci 4% > Jobs 3%, was blocked), so the order above #12 relies on the gut-check moves.
